criteria.evidence: Nameable as 'cold-chain corporate navy': deep navy plus ice blue on an almost-white ground, geometric sans, hairline rules, uppercase tracked eyebrow labels and numbered rails (01 / YOUR REQUIREMENTS).
Headings are very dark and heavy, body copy mid-gray, eyebrows small and light; the navy process band and the photo card would still read as the two heaviest objects with colour removed.

Split hero with photo card, then a divided logo row, a tinted form panel, an icon-card trio, a dark map panel beside a route grid, a full-width dark three-step band, a two-column accordion, a carrier panel, then the footer.
Hero is a left/right split: stacked headline and two buttons on the left, a rounded photo of a liveried refrigerated truck on the right with a navy caption bar laid over its lower edge.
A real photograph of a Volvo FH tractor pulling an FWL-branded reefer trailer, the FWL globe logo in header and footer, and three real client logos.
Under 'Our clients' the three marks are actual logo artwork - the Danone star-and-child, the red Shin-Line seal, the red HAMLE swoosh - not typeset names.
A quote form with From / To city fields, a cargo-and-quantity field, a temperature field and a date picker; plus an FAQ accordion, a language switcher and a light/dark toggle.
'Your route. / Our solution.' is set genuinely large and tight, and the eyebrow labels ('WHERE WE OPERATE', '01 / DOMESTIC') are genuinely tiny and widely tracked.
Palette is navy, mid-blue and near-white throughout; no violet or purple-blue wash anywhere, including the dark band and the map panel.
No blur, glow or abstract 3D; the one illustration is a labelled route diagram on a dotted grid with named nodes - Europe, Russia, Kazakhstan, CIS countries, Central Asia.
Icons are monochrome navy glyphs in pale rounded tiles - snowflake, thermometer, phone handset, arrows - with no colour-emoji rendering.
Saturated blue is confined to the filled buttons, the link arrows and the second headline line; everything else is navy text on near-white.
Most sections share one near-white ground separated by hairlines, with contrast coming from decided objects - the pale-blue quote and carrier panels and the full-width navy process band.
Besides cards there is a divided logo row, an inline form, a dark full-bleed band with numbered columns, a rule-separated accordion and a large dark map panel.

Names a phone number (+7 708 180 5200), named corridors (Kazakhstan-Russia, Kazakhstan-Europe, CIS countries-Kazakhstan), named clients, and cargo examples like 'dairy products, 12 tonnes' and '+2...+6 C'.
No lorem and no invented counters - the page makes no '500+ trucks' or '99% on time' claim; the only placeholder text sits inside form inputs where it belongs.

The page closes on a carrier-recruitment panel - 'Have a refrigerated truck? Let's work together.' with an 'Offer your truck' button and a three-point list of what to send - a different ask from the header's 'Find a truck'.
Wide consistent outer margins, air above each section label, copy columns held well short of full width; nothing is crammed against an edge.

The running order - split hero, logo strip, icon-tile card trio, numbered three-step band, FAQ accordion, closing CTA panel - is the stock B2B services template, and the icon-in-rounded-tile card is its most recognisable part.

The hero stacks two competing headlines in two colours, two of three cargo cards carry the identical snowflake icon, the client logos are unnormalised, and the date field shows native browser chrome next to custom inputs.

defects.what: The hero has two headlines, not one: 'Need a refrigerated truck?' in near-black and 'The right truck for your cargo.' in blue, at the same size and weight, so nothing is primary and the colour split reads as decoration rather than hierarchy.
defects.where: Hero, left column above the two buttons

defects.what: Client logos are placed at their native colour and weight - a red seal, a red slab wordmark, a blue figure - so the row becomes the loudest thing on the page and fights the navy system; no grayscale or common-height treatment.
defects.where: 'Our clients' strip between hero and quote form

defects.what: Two card grids run close together with near-identical cards (white, thin border, title, bottom link with arrow), and five of the six route cards repeat the same link label 'Discuss this route', so each card carries almost no information.
defects.where: 'What do you need to ship?' trio and the 'Choose your route' six-card grid

defects.what: Two of the three cargo cards use the same snowflake icon, so the icon column no longer distinguishes chilled from frozen.
defects.where: 'What do you need to ship?' - 'Chilled products' and 'Frozen cargo' cards

defects.what: Utility controls take prime space: a theme toggle sits beside the main CTA and the language switcher gets its own full-width strip under the nav, a second bar competing with the header before the page has said anything.
defects.where: Header and the language strip directly beneath it

defects.what: The FAQ shows only three questions and its left column is left largely empty under the heading and phone number, so a full-width section carries very little.
The date field renders native browser chrome - grey 'dd/mm/yyyy' and a system calendar button - alongside custom-styled text inputs in the same form.
defects.where: Quote form, 'When do you need a truck?'

defects.what: A '01 - 06' counter sits beside 'Choose your route' as if the grid paginated, but all six cards are visible at once.
The quote form's only submit is 'Get a quote on WhatsApp'; the form offers no email or callback path, and the caveat about the message opening elsewhere is set in the smallest type on the page.

aesthetic_in_one_phrase: Cold-chain corporate navy - deep navy and ice blue on near-white, geometric sans, hairline rules and numbered rails
